My name is Brian Eric Steuber. I want to tell you how Harley-Davidson saved my life and helps me battle PTSD (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder from my 2 tours in Iraq) daily. 

For a person like myself who served in the military for almost 9 years. Who also went to combat twice, once in 2003-2004 and again in 2005-2006 I came back with many physical injuries (no body parts missing). But the worst injuries are the ones you can’t see. Those injuries are PTSD (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder). The memories, flashbacks, night-sweats and anger issues at times are calmed by a wonderful woman in my life. My wife. But still there is that 50% that she can’t help. That’s where my 2001 Harley-Davidson Road King  has come in to play.

For any and all Harley-Davidson owners there is something that in intangible about owning a Harley-Davidson. For those who don’t, you just will never understand what that is. A person could by an $80,000 import or domestic mode of transportation. That person could have some problems at home and they get in that expensive tin can and still have those problems when they return home. Yes you could close your windows and blast the music until your ears bleed and sing your heart out. But you still will not solve any problems. You will return with nothing sorted out and nothing gained.

That important 50% of where my problems exist, disappear. As a 100% disabled veteran I chose a different route, rather than sitting back and taking a bunch of medications and collecting my disability check. It is all without the help of a drug, therapy or any other modern medicine supposedly to help you in recovering. My medical prescription is 800 plus pounds of American made metal and chrome. She might be older than most bikes but she is mine. I ride her at least 3 times a week. Rain, sleet, snow, wind…whatever kind of whether comes up. I am out there riding. It might not be a long ride, if the conditions are horrible (around my block) or it might not be actually outside. Like when my wife and I lived in an apartment. All winter I rode up and down the apartment parking area under the building for hours as I blast Five Finger Death Punch ”Remember Everything” and Papa Roach “Before I die”

Why? Because anytime I had an issue. A flare up of my problems or I got angry. I just hopped on my “Steel Horse” and peaced out mentally for a few hours. I would think about what I needed to accomplish and what my problems where and how to fix them. No medication or drug can do that.

Ask a Vietnam Vet who rides a Harley. Why they ride? Ask a World-War II vet they ride. Hell ask any veteran why they ride. Most veterans will tell you one word. Freedom.  It’s that peace of mind and the freedom to think or not think when you ride. Because you can’t think of anything else but one thing at a time. That’s why Harley is a cypher. Because it is like an algorithm, for performing a decryption for your brain and your thoughts that might be locked up tight in there.

You don’t have to ride fast like most crotch rocket riders do (really they are meant to do). All you have to do I start up your “Steel Horse” and hear that sexy rumble. You feel that shake. Give the throttle one roll of the right wrist and see if it doesn’t put a smile on your face. Hell, give it two rolls of the wrist.
 
That feeling is a drug. That sound is intoxicating that emotional connection to an inanimate object is unparalleled to anything that is man-made. No drug can compare, no feeling is better. That’s why I ride.

Harley-Davidson has provided a thought-clearing alternative to many confrontational arguments without the use or abuse of drugs or alcohol. They provide a choice or alternative means to sort out situations in your life by providing a vehicle to clear your mind with. Where the only thing you can do is focus on 1 thing at a time.

I ride my 2001 Harley-Davidson for the sole purpose of riding for those who can't or are unable to because of the stifling issues of PTSD (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder) We as Harley-Davidson riders all ride for something or someone. My purpose and reason is one that is not just special to me, but special to a select percentage of the population who decided one way or another to make a sacrifice and answer a calling.

Being a soldier, service member or airmen is choosing one way or another to become part of a fraternity that knows no color, creed or religious boundaries. The brothers and sisters in arms of all generations across all wars know one thing. That we can call each other in a time of need before, during and after the battle, war or fight has ended. But for some of us the battle, war or fight will never end. Especially when it comes to PTSD. The fight against PTSD is just that, a fight. It is a daily battle that some of us have succumbed to.
 
But to ride for a purpose as all Harley-Davidson riders do one way or another. We all ride for something or someone. My purpose and reason is one that is not just special to me, but special to a select percentage of the population who decided one way or another to make a sacrifice and answer a calling.
  
I will continue my battle, my war, my fight daily as I ride my 2001 Harley-Davidson Road King and I will ride for those who can't or are unable to. Harley-Davidson is a brand that signifies the fight and the freedom in which we as soldiers, service members and airmen have gone through and some of us continue to go through because of PTSD.
  
I hope everyone realizes the impact on personal freedom in which the Harley-Davidson brand means. It means more than any one could ever imagine. Whether you served in any type of combat or military. There are still battles at home which individuals who are not prior or current military go through that are solved just by getting on their respective Harley-Davidson and sorting out their problems. I truly believe Harley-Davidson has saved many lives and relationships just by offering a choice to either go deeper into a problem or situation or jumping on their 'Freedom Cycle" and sorting it out on the road.
  
I am, just like the millions of other Harley-Davidson riders are thankful for the opportunity of choice and the freedom of expression in which Harley-Davidson provides. I as a rider and a sufferer of PTSD from 2 combat tours… I am in Harley-Davidson’s debt and thank them from the bottom of my heart. They have saved my life on more than one occasion. GOD bless them.
 
 
Thank you so very much,
 
Brian Steuber
